title: Polity Lec 2
summary: DPSPs are in Part IV (Articles 36-51), inspired by Ireland; non-justiciable but fundamental in governance (Article 37).
DPSPs aim at social and economic democracy (a 'novel feature' - Ambedkar); Fundamental Rights establish political democracy and are negative obligations, DPSPs are positive obligations.
The Socialist/Gandhian/Liberal-Intellectual classification is not written in the Constitution.
Article 39(a)-(f): livelihood, distribution of resources, preventing concentration of wealth, equal pay, workers' health, child development - trick 'LDC goes to PHC'.

Article 40 panchayats, 41 work/public assistance, 42 work conditions and maternity relief, 43 living wage/cottage industries, 44 UCC, 45 early childhood care, 46 SC/ST, 47 prohibition/nutrition, 48 agriculture and animal husbandry, 48A environment, 49 monuments, 50 separation of judiciary from executive, 51 international peace.
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 4 DPSPs: 39A, 39(f), 43A, 48A; the 44th added 38(2); the 97th added 43B; the 86th changed the subject of Article 45.
Uttarakhand is the first state to implement a UCC; Goa follows the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.
FR vs DPSP: Champakam (1951) FR supreme; Golaknath 1967; 24th and 25th (Art. 31C) Amendments 1971; Kesavananda 1973 basic structure; 42nd gave DPSP primacy; Minerva Mills 1980 restored balance.
Maneka Gandhi (1978) recognised 'due process'; Gopalan upheld 'procedure established by law'; the 39th Amendment is linked to the Raj Narain case.
Fundamental Duties: Part IVA, Article 51A, 42nd Amendment 1976, borrowed from the USSR, Swaran Singh Committee; increased from 10 to 11 (86th Amendment, 2002, Vajpayee).
Trick A-K: Abide, Bapu, Three (sovereignty-unity-integrity), Defend, Equality, Fort, Greenery, Humanism, Violence (I), Jadeja (excellence), Kids.
Justice Verma Committee (constituted 1998, report 1999); Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, 30 are available only to citizens.
Official Language: Part XVII, Articles 343-351; 343 Hindi in Devanagari, 344 Commission, 345-347 regional, 348-349 courts, 350 grievances, 350A/B (7th Amendment 1956), 351 promotion of Hindi.
Eighth Schedule: 14 to 22 languages; Sindhi (21st, 1967), KNM (71st, 1992), BDSM (92nd, 2003), Oriya renamed Odia (96th, 2011); language families: Indo-European ~73%, Dravidian ~20%.

mcqs.q: In which Part of the Constitution are the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) contained?
mcqs.e: DPSPs are in Part IV (Articles 36-51); Fundamental Rights are in Part III.

mcqs.q: DPSPs are contained in which Articles?
mcqs.e: Articles 36-51 = Directive Principles of State Policy.

mcqs.q: What is the basic objective of the DPSPs?
mcqs.e: DPSPs are directions to the State to build a welfare state.

mcqs.q: The DPSPs of the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of which country?
mcqs.e: DPSPs were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

mcqs.q: What is the nature of the DPSPs?
mcqs.e: DPSPs cannot be enforced in court but are fundamental in governance.

mcqs.q: Which Article gives the right to move the Supreme Court for violation of Fundamental Rights?
mcqs.e: Article 32 for the Supreme Court; Article 226 for High Courts.

mcqs.q: Under which Article does a High Court issue writs for the protection of Fundamental Rights?
mcqs.e: High Court writ jurisdiction is wider: covers legal rights as well as Fundamental Rights.

mcqs.q: Why is the writ jurisdiction of a High Court considered wider than that of the Supreme Court?
o: It issues writs only for DPSPs
It has no power to issue writs
It issues writs only during an Emergency
It can issue writs for legal rights as well as Fundamental Rights
mcqs.e: The scope of Article 226 is wider than that of Article 32.

mcqs.q: The concept of writs (Habeas Corpus etc.) in India is borrowed from which country?
mcqs.e: The writs come from Britain, as do single citizenship, parliamentary system, FPTP and bicameralism.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a writ?
mcqs.e: The five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Habeas Corpus'?
o: To have the body (produce the body)
mcqs.e: Habeas Corpus = 'to have the body of'; a remedy against unlawful detention.

mcqs.q: How did Dr. Ambedkar describe the DPSPs?
mcqs.e: He called DPSPs a 'novel feature'; Article 32 he called the heart and soul of the Constitution.

mcqs.q: The DPSPs resemble the 'Instrument of Instructions' contained in which Act?
mcqs.e: According to Ambedkar, DPSPs are like the Instrument of Instructions of the 1935 Act.

mcqs.q: Fundamental Rights establish which type of democracy?
mcqs.e: Fundamental Rights = political democracy; DPSPs = social and economic democracy.

mcqs.q: DPSPs aim at establishing which type of democracy?
mcqs.e: Preventing concentration of wealth and discrimination is the goal of DPSPs.

mcqs.q: What kind of obligation do Fundamental Rights impose on the State?
mcqs.e: Rights like Article 15 restrain the State from discriminating; DPSPs are positive obligations.

mcqs.q: What kind of obligation do DPSPs impose on the State?
mcqs.e: DPSPs ask the State to do certain things.

mcqs.q: Where is the Socialist, Gandhian and Liberal-Intellectual classification of DPSPs written?
mcqs.e: This classification was made by scholars; the Constitution does not mention it.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a DPSP?
o: Promotion of cottage industries in rural areas
mcqs.e: There is no DPSP on corporate farming; cottage industries are in Article 43.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for the promotion of cottage industries in rural areas?
mcqs.e: Article 43: living wage and cottage industries (Gandhian part).

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for participation of workers in the management of industries?
mcqs.e: Article 43A was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

mcqs.q: What does Article 43 provide for?
o: Living wage and decent conditions of work
mcqs.e: Living wage is socialist and cottage industries Gandhian in nature.

mcqs.q: In the context of DPSPs, the meaning of 'State' is the same as in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 36 adopts the same definition of 'State' as Article 12.

mcqs.q: Which Article defines 'State' for the purposes of DPSPs?
mcqs.e: Article 36 defines the State.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT included in 'State' under Article 12?
mcqs.e: Parliament, State Legislatures, Union and State Governments and local bodies are 'State'.

mcqs.q: Which Article deals with the application of DPSPs?
mcqs.e: Article 37: DPSPs are not enforceable by any court but are fundamental in governance.

mcqs.q: Which Article talks about minimising inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities?
mcqs.e: Article 38(2) stresses reducing inequalities.

mcqs.q: Article 38(2) was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
mcqs.e: The 44th Amendment (Janata government) added Article 38(2).

mcqs.q: Which Article speaks of a social order based on social, economic and political justice?
mcqs.e: Article 38(1): social order for the welfare of the people.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for equal justice and free legal aid to the poor?
mcqs.e: Article 39A was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

mcqs.q: Equal pay for equal work for both men and women is part of which Article?
mcqs.e: 39(d): equal pay for equal work (socialist).

mcqs.q: How many clauses (a to f) does Article 39 have?
mcqs.e: 39(a) to 39(f); memory trick: LDC goes to PHC.

mcqs.q: What does Article 39(a) provide?
o: Right of men and women to an adequate means of livelihood
mcqs.e: 39(a) = right to livelihood for men and women.

mcqs.q: 'Equitable distribution of material resources' is in which clause?
mcqs.e: 39(b) = distribution of material resources to subserve the common good.

mcqs.q: Preventing concentration of wealth and means of production is in which clause?
mcqs.e: 39(c): the economic system should not result in concentration of wealth.

mcqs.q: Protection of the health of workers and of children from abuse is in which clause?
mcqs.e: 39(e) = health and strength of workers and tender age of children.

mcqs.q: Opportunities for the healthy development of children (in conditions of freedom and dignity) are in which clause?
mcqs.e: 39(f) was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for the organisation of village panchayats?
mcqs.e: Article 40 is a Gandhian DPSP.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides the right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases?
mcqs.e: Public assistance in unemployment, old age, sickness etc. - Article 41.

mcqs.q: Just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief are provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 42: just and humane conditions of work, maternity relief.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for the promotion of co-operative societies?
mcqs.e: Article 43B was added by the 97th Amendment, 2011.

mcqs.q: Article 43B was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
mcqs.e: The 97th Amendment also added Part IXB (Co-operative Societies).

mcqs.q: The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Memory trick: 44 has two identical fours = uniform.

mcqs.q: Which is the first state after Independence to fully implement a UCC?
mcqs.e: Uttarakhand is the first; Goa follows the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.

mcqs.q: Which civil code is in force in Goa?
mcqs.e: The pre-liberation Portuguese Civil Code of 1867 still applies in Goa.

mcqs.q: Early childhood care (0-6 years) is provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: The 86th Amendment, 2002 changed the subject matter of Article 45.

mcqs.q: What did the 86th Amendment, 2002 do with Article 45?
o: Changed its content and added the right to education as Article 21A
mcqs.e: Education for 6-14 years moved to Article 21A; Article 45 now covers care up to 6 years.

mcqs.q: Promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 46 is a Gandhian DPSP.

mcqs.q: Prohibition of intoxicating drinks/drugs and raising the level of nutrition and standard of living is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 47: nutrition, standard of living, public health and prohibition.

mcqs.q: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry on modern lines is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 48 (Gandhian) - also covers prohibition of cow slaughter.

mcqs.q: Protection of the environment, forests and wildlife is in which Article?
mcqs.e: 48A was added by the 42nd Amendment; 51A(g) is a citizen's duty.

mcqs.q: Protection of monuments, places and objects of national importance is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 49: protection of monuments.

mcqs.q: Separation of the judiciary from the executive is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 50: keeping judiciary and executive separate (liberal-intellectual).

mcqs.q: Promotion of international peace and security is in which Article?
mcqs.e: Memory trick: offer Rs 51 as prasad and pray for peace.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a provision of Article 51?
o: Just and honourable relations between nations
Respect for international law and treaty obligations
mcqs.e: Protection of forests and wildlife is in Article 48A.

mcqs.q: Which is true about 'providing safe drinking water' or 'granting religious freedom' as DPSPs?
mcqs.e: Religious freedom is a Fundamental Right (Articles 25-28), not a DPSP.

mcqs.q: According to Article 13, a law that violates Fundamental Rights shall be:
mcqs.e: The power of judicial review flows from Article 13.

mcqs.q: How many new DPSP provisions were added by the 42nd Amendment?
mcqs.e: 39A, 39(f), 43A and 48A (trick: poor workers' children and environment).

mcqs.q: Which DPSP was NOT added by the 42nd Amendment?
mcqs.e: 43B was added by the 97th Amendment.

mcqs.q: What did the 86th Amendment do with regard to DPSPs?
o: Changed the subject matter of Article 45
mcqs.e: The 86th changed Article 45; it added no new DPSP.

mcqs.q: Which judicial doctrine saves laws promoting DPSPs from being struck down for violating Fundamental Rights, by interpreting both in harmony?
mcqs.e: FRs and DPSPs are read together in harmony.

mcqs.q: Only the unconstitutional part of a law is struck down, not the whole law - what is this doctrine called?
mcqs.e: Linked to Article 13: cut off the rotten limb, do not kill the body.

mcqs.q: A pre-Constitution law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights becomes dormant but can revive if the inconsistency is removed - this is the:
mcqs.e: The law is overshadowed, not dead; it revives once the conflicting FR is amended.

mcqs.q: The 'Doctrine of Eclipse' is associated with which Article?
mcqs.e: It applies to pre-Constitution laws (before 26 January 1950).

mcqs.q: Which 1931 resolution inspired India's Directive Principles?
mcqs.e: The 1931 Karachi session passed resolutions on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Policy.

mcqs.q: Who presided over the 1931 Karachi session of the Congress?
mcqs.e: The Karachi Resolution covered Fundamental Rights and National Economic Policy.

mcqs.q: What did the court hold in the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951)?
o: DPSPs are superior to Fundamental Rights
Fundamental Rights are superior to DPSPs
mcqs.e: The case concerned caste-based reservation; FR prevail over DPSP.

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court decide in the Shankari Prasad case (1951)?
o: Parliament can change the basic structure
mcqs.e: Shankari Prasad (1951): FRs can be amended under Article 368.

mcqs.q: In which year was Golaknath v. State of Punjab decided?
mcqs.e: It held that Fundamental Rights cannot be amended.

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court hold in the Golaknath case (1967)?
mcqs.e: Golaknath reversed the view taken in Shankari Prasad.

mcqs.q: In response to Golaknath, which 1971 amendment declared that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights?
mcqs.e: The 24th Amendment, 1971 amended Articles 13 and 368.

mcqs.q: Article 31C was added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Added under Indira Gandhi; shielded laws implementing 39(b) and (c) from Articles 14 and 19.

mcqs.q: Under the original Article 31C, laws implementing which DPSPs could not be challenged?
mcqs.e: They could not be challenged on grounds of Articles 14, 19 and 31.

mcqs.q: When was the right to property removed from the list of Fundamental Rights?
mcqs.e: It is now a legal right under Article 300A.

mcqs.q: What did the 26th Amendment, 1971 do?
mcqs.e: Indira Gandhi ended privy purses paid to former princely rulers.

mcqs.q: The Ninth Schedule and Articles 31A and 31B were added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Mainly to protect land reform laws from judicial challenge.

mcqs.q: In which year was the Kesavananda Bharati case decided?
mcqs.e: On 24 April 1973, by a 13-judge bench.

mcqs.q: How many judges sat on the bench in the Kesavananda Bharati case?
mcqs.e: The largest constitutional bench so far.

mcqs.q: The Basic Structure doctrine originated from which case?
mcqs.e: The term 'basic structure' is not written anywhere in the Constitution.

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court say about Parliament's amending power in Kesavananda Bharati?
o: Fundamental Rights can be amended but not the basic structure
mcqs.e: Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure.

mcqs.q: Which case is known as the 'Ninth Schedule case'?
mcqs.e: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review.

mcqs.q: What did the 42nd Amendment (1976) do regarding DPSPs and Fundamental Rights?
o: Gave Fundamental Rights primacy over DPSPs
Gave all DPSPs primacy over Fundamental Rights (Articles 14, 19, 31)
mcqs.e: The 42nd Amendment is called the 'Mini Constitution'.

mcqs.q: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment is known as the:
mcqs.e: Enacted in 1976 under Indira Gandhi.

mcqs.q: Which amendment undid many provisions of the 42nd Amendment?
mcqs.e: Passed under the Janata Party government in 1978.

mcqs.q: 'The Constitution is founded on the bedrock of balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs' - this was held in which case?
mcqs.e: Minerva Mills Ltd. was a Karnataka company; the court upheld balance between the two.

mcqs.q: Which case struck down the 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C to all DPSPs, restoring the primacy of Fundamental Rights?
mcqs.e: Minerva Mills (1980) held that DPSPs cannot override Articles 14 and 19 wholesale.

mcqs.q: Which amendment is associated with the Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain case?
mcqs.e: It put elections of the President, VP, PM and Speaker beyond judicial review.

mcqs.q: From which constituency did Raj Narain contest against Indira Gandhi?
mcqs.e: The Allahabad High Court set aside Indira Gandhi's election.

mcqs.q: Which concept did the court accept in the A.K. Gopalan case?
mcqs.e: At that time the Supreme Court did not recognise 'due process'.

mcqs.q: In which case was 'Due Process of Law' first recognised in India?
mcqs.e: It is an American concept; Article 21 says 'procedure established by law'.

mcqs.q: The concept of 'procedure established by law' is borrowed from which country's Constitution?
mcqs.e: This narrower concept in Article 21 was taken from Japan.

mcqs.q: In the Maneka Gandhi case, which right was held to be a Fundamental Right?
o: Right to travel abroad and return
mcqs.e: Under Article 21; the law must be 'just, fair and reasonable'.

mcqs.q: In which Part of the Constitution are the Fundamental Duties?
mcqs.e: Part IVA contains only Article 51A.

mcqs.q: Fundamental Duties are given in which Article?
mcqs.e: All Fundamental Duties are in a single Article, 51A.

mcqs.q: Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) were added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Added under Indira Gandhi, during the Emergency.

mcqs.q: India's Fundamental Duties are borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
mcqs.e: Inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR.

mcqs.q: On whose recommendation were the Fundamental Duties added?
mcqs.e: Swaran Singh was a minister in Indira Gandhi's cabinet.

mcqs.q: How many Fundamental Duties did the Swaran Singh Committee recommend?
mcqs.e: It suggested 8, but the 42nd Amendment included 10 duties.

mcqs.q: Which recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee was NOT accepted by the government?
o: Penalty for non-performance of duties / duty to pay taxes
mcqs.e: Duty to pay taxes and penalties for non-compliance were not included.

mcqs.q: How many Fundamental Duties were originally added by the 42nd Amendment?
mcqs.e: The 11th duty was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002.

mcqs.q: How many Fundamental Duties are there at present?
mcqs.e: The 11th duty was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002.

mcqs.q: The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: During Atal Bihari Vajpayee's tenure.

mcqs.q: Under the 11th Fundamental Duty (Article 51A(k)), who shall provide opportunities for education to a child aged 6-14?
mcqs.e: Trick: K = Kids; parents/guardians must send children to school.

mcqs.q: What is a citizen's duty under Article 51A(a)?
o: Abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and National Anthem
mcqs.e: Trick: A = Abide / Anthem.

mcqs.q: What is the duty under Article 51A(b)?
o: To cherish and follow the noble ideals of the freedom struggle
mcqs.e: Trick: B = Bapu / Bhagat Singh.

mcqs.q: Upholding the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: C = three things (sovereignty, unity, integrity).

mcqs.q: Defending the country and rendering national service when called upon is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: D = Defend.

mcqs.q: Promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all the people of India is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: E = Equality (harmony, brotherhood).

mcqs.q: Renouncing practices derogatory to the dignity of women is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Remember both duties with E = Equality.

mcqs.q: Valuing and preserving the rich heritage of our composite culture is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: F = Fort (fort = culture).

mcqs.q: Protecting and improving the natural environment (forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife) is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: G = Greenery.

mcqs.q: Developing scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: H = Humanism.

mcqs.q: Safeguarding public property and abjuring violence is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: I = 'showing eyes' = violence.

mcqs.q: Striving towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity is in which clause?
mcqs.e: Trick: J = Jadeja (excellent in every field).

mcqs.q: What is Article 51A(k) about?
o: Providing educational opportunities to children aged 6 to 14
mcqs.e: K = Kids.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Article 48A and Article 51A(g)?
o: 48A is a citizen's duty, 51A(g) the State's
48A is the State's obligation, 51A(g) a citizen's duty
mcqs.e: Environment: State - 48A (DPSP); citizens - 51A(g) (Fundamental Duty).

mcqs.q: When was the Justice Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties set up and when did it report?
mcqs.e: It identified existing laws enforcing duties and advised including them in education.

mcqs.q: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 helps enforce which Fundamental Duty?
o: Respect for the Constitution, National Flag and National Anthem (51A(a))
mcqs.e: Punishes insult to national symbols.

mcqs.q: The Wildlife (Protection) Act helps enforce which Fundamental Duty?
mcqs.e: G = Greenery.

mcqs.q: For whom are Fundamental Duties meant?
mcqs.e: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and apply only to citizens.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Fundamental Rights are available only to Indian citizens?
mcqs.e: The remaining Fundamental Rights are available to both citizens and foreigners.

mcqs.q: What is the nature of Fundamental Duties?
mcqs.e: The Constitution provides no direct penalty for non-performance of duties.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT linked to Article 51A(h)?
o: Safeguarding public property and abjuring violence
mcqs.e: Public property and non-violence are in 51A(i).

mcqs.q: Which Part of the Constitution deals with the Official Language of the Union?
mcqs.e: Official Language: Part XVII, Articles 343-351.

mcqs.q: Which Articles deal with the Official Language?
mcqs.e: Part XVII has four chapters.

mcqs.q: What has been declared the Official Language of the Union?
mcqs.e: Article 343(1).

mcqs.q: Under Article 343, English was to be used for how many years?
mcqs.e: The Official Languages Act extended it; English continues to be used today.

mcqs.q: Article 344 relates to:
o: Official Language Commission and Committee of Parliament
mcqs.e: The President constitutes the Official Language Commission.

mcqs.q: Who constitutes the Official Language Commission?
mcqs.e: Under Article 344.

mcqs.q: Chapter I of Part XVII deals with:
mcqs.e: Ch. II regional languages (345-347); Ch. III courts (348-349); Ch. IV special directives (350-351).

mcqs.q: Regional languages are dealt with in which Articles of Part XVII?
mcqs.e: Chapter II: regional languages.

mcqs.q: Which Article empowers a State Legislature to adopt one or more languages as the official language of the State?
mcqs.e: Article 345: official language of a State.

mcqs.q: The language for communication between states, or between a state and the Union, is dealt with in which Article?
mcqs.e: Article 346.

mcqs.q: The language of the Supreme Court and High Courts is dealt with in which Articles?
mcqs.e: Chapter III: language of the courts; mainly English.

mcqs.q: Who can authorise the use of Hindi/a regional language in a High Court in addition to English?
mcqs.e: English is used in the Supreme Court.

mcqs.q: Which Article gives the right to submit a grievance in any language used in the Union or a State?
mcqs.e: Article 350 (Chapter IV: special directives).

mcqs.q: Facilities for primary education in the mother tongue for linguistic minority children are provided in which Article?
mcqs.e: 350A: directive to local authorities.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for a Special Officer for linguistic minorities?
mcqs.e: The Special Officer is appointed by the President.

mcqs.q: Who appoints the Special Officer for linguistic minorities?
mcqs.e: Article 350B.

mcqs.q: Articles 350A and 350B were added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Added at the time of states' reorganisation.

mcqs.q: Which Article contains the directive for the spread and development of Hindi?
mcqs.e: Directs the Union to promote the spread of Hindi.

mcqs.q: Article 351 gives a directive to whom?
mcqs.e: Developing Hindi is a duty of the Union.

mcqs.q: Directives outside Part IV (special directives) are found in which part of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: These are directives not contained in Part IV.

mcqs.q: How many languages were originally in the Eighth Schedule?
mcqs.e: At present there are 22 languages.

mcqs.q: How many languages are there in the Eighth Schedule at present?
mcqs.e: 22 languages after the 92nd Amendment, 2003.

mcqs.q: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Sindhi was added in 1967.

mcqs.q: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Trick: KNM = Konkani, Nepali, Manipuri.

mcqs.q: Bodo, Dogri, Santhali and Maithili were added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: Trick: BDSM = Bodo, Dogri, Santhali, Maithili.

mcqs.q: What did the 96th Amendment, 2011 do to the Eighth Schedule?
mcqs.e: No new language was added.

mcqs.q: Which Eighth Schedule language belongs to the Tibeto-Burman family?
mcqs.e: Bodo is spoken in the Assam region.

mcqs.q: Where is Konkani mainly spoken?
mcqs.e: Konkani belongs to the Indo-Aryan family.

mcqs.q: Santhali is mainly spoken in which region?
mcqs.e: Santhali belongs to the Austroasiatic family.

mcqs.q: Maithili is mainly the language of which region?
mcqs.e: Maithili belongs to the Indo-Aryan family.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest autonomous council in Assam, associated with the Bodo language?
mcqs.e: Sixth Schedule states: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.

mcqs.q: Which states are covered under the Sixth Schedule?
mcqs.e: Trick: ATM - Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya, Mizoram.

mcqs.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Mizoram?
mcqs.e: Mizo is Tibeto-Burman; Ao is a language of Nagaland.

mcqs.q: The Ao language is associated with which state?
mcqs.e: Ao is the language of the Ao Naga tribe.

mcqs.q: The most widely spoken languages in India belong to which language family?
mcqs.e: About three-quarters of the population; Hindi belongs to this family.

mcqs.q: The languages of South India (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam) belong to which family?
mcqs.e: About 20% of the population.

mcqs.q: Sanskrit belongs to which language family?
mcqs.e: Sanskrit belongs to the Indo-Aryan branch.

mcqs.q: Austric family languages are mainly spoken in which part of India?
mcqs.e: Santhali (Jharkhand) and Khasi (Meghalaya) belong to this family.

mcqs.q: Sino-Tibetan languages are mainly spoken in which region?
mcqs.e: Bodo, Mizo etc. belong to this family.

mcqs.q: Which of the following statements about Sanskrit is correct?
o: It is the national language of India
It is the root of all Indian languages
It is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution
It was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment
mcqs.e: Sanskrit was among the original 14 languages; India has no national language.

mcqs.q: Has the Indian Constitution declared any national language?
o: No, it only provides for official languages
mcqs.e: The Constitution speaks only of official languages (343-351).

mcqs.q: When was the Official Language Commission to be constituted?
mcqs.e: Under Article 344, constituted by the President.

mcqs.q: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution relates to:
mcqs.e: A total of 22 languages.

mcqs.q: What is mainly the language of proceedings in the Supreme Court?
mcqs.e: Article 348(1).

mcqs.q: Which of the following DPSPs is purely Gandhian in nature?
mcqs.e: Panchayats, cottage industries, co-operatives, SC/ST upliftment, prohibition, agriculture - Gandhian.

mcqs.q: Which of the following DPSPs falls in the Liberal-Intellectual category?
mcqs.e: UCC, separation of judiciary, international peace, monuments - liberal-intellectual.

mcqs.q: Which of the following DPSPs belongs to the Socialist category?
o: Article 39(d) - equal pay for equal work
mcqs.e: DPSPs on workers and inequality are socialist.

mcqs.q: Which statement about DPSPs is correct?
o: They can be enforced under Article 32
They cannot be enforced by a citizen through a writ petition
mcqs.e: DPSPs are non-enforceable but fundamental in governance.

mcqs.q: What did Dr. Ambedkar call Article 32?
o: Heart and soul of the Constitution
mcqs.e: Right to Constitutional Remedies.

mcqs.q: The 1971 amendment declaring that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights was passed under which Prime Minister?
mcqs.e: The 24th and 25th Amendments were passed in 1971.

mcqs.q: Clause (k), the 11th Fundamental Duty, was added under which Prime Minister?
mcqs.e: 86th Amendment, 2002; the other 10 were added under Indira Gandhi.

mcqs.q: Which Fundamental Right was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002?
mcqs.e: Right to elementary education.

mcqs.q: In the trick 'LDC goes to PHC' for Article 39, what does 'L' (clause (a)) stand for?
mcqs.e: L-D-C: Livelihood, Distribution, Concentration; P-H-C: Pay, Health, Children.

mcqs.q: In the trick 'LDC goes to PHC', what does 'P' stand for?
mcqs.e: 39(d) = equal pay for equal work.

mcqs.q: What was the memory trick suggested for Article 51 (peace)?
o: Offer Rs 51 as prasad and pray for peace
mcqs.e: Article 51 = international peace.
